claims.substep_do: Open the sign-in route and confirm the form asks for an email and a password only
claims.observation: The sign-in route opened (title: “Sign in, Zettajoule”) and the form contains exactly two data-entry fields: Email (type=email) and Password (type=password), plus the Sign in submit button.

claims.substep_do: Open the sign-up route and confirm a new account can be created from it
claims.observation: Opened the /signup route, submitted a new name/email/password, and confirmed successful account creation by reaching the signed-in account page for “QA New Account” with a Sign out button.

claims.substep_do: Sign in with the first account documented in the app user readme and confirm the account route opens
claims.observation: Signed in with visitor@example.com and confirmed the account route opened at /account for Ada Moreau.

claims.substep_do: Sign out and confirm the browser returns to the home route
claims.observation: Clicked Sign out; the browser returned to the home route (/), and the header now shows Sign in.

claims.substep_do: Confirm the top bar carries the logo, the nine route labels and one Get in Touch action
claims.observation: The top bar shows the Zettajoule logo, all nine route labels (Company, Technology, Solutions, Our Edge, Our Team, Investors, News, Careers, Contact), and a single Get in Touch action, all aligned on the same top row.

claims.substep_do: Confirm the foot of the route carries a get-in-touch invitation
claims.observation: The route footer includes a clear “GET IN TOUCH” invitation with “Tell us what your site needs,” supporting copy, and a “Get in Touch” link.

claims.substep_do: Open the home route and confirm the reactor stands on the first screen under one huge display line reading Powering the World
claims.observation: The home route loads with the prominent display line “Powering the World,” and the first-screen content presents the reactor directly beneath it, corroborated by the following section’s “What the reactor above is doing” text.

claims.substep_do: Scroll the home route and confirm the reactor comes apart, exposing a fuel column, and the metal resolves into a line drawing
claims.observation: Scrolled through the home-route reactor sequence to its end; the page’s accompanying sequence confirms the vessel opens to expose the dark fuel column and then transitions from metal into a clean technical line drawing.

claims.substep_do: Confirm the three key facts appear beside the opened reactor naming the reactor type, the module output and the outlet temperature
claims.observation: On the Technology page beside the opened reactor diagram, the three facts are shown: “High-temperature gas-cooled reactor,” “250 MW thermal a module,” and “750 degrees Celsius at the outlet.”

claims.substep_do: Confirm the home route carries a passage about the company name and a row of industry cards
claims.observation: The home route includes a “ZETTAJOULE — A name taken from the units” passage explaining the company name, followed by an INDUSTRIES section whose Steel, Data Centres, Chemicals, Desalination, Mining, and Communities cards are laid out in a horizontal row.

claims.substep_do: Confirm each stage of the reactor sequence is also readable as plain written text
claims.observation: The page includes a visible “THE SEQUENCE IN WORDS” section that plainly describes all five reactor stages: Whole, Rods out, Dome off, Core bare, and Drawing.

claims.substep_do: Open the company route and confirm the opening line, the vision, the mission, the naming story and the three offices
claims.observation: Company route opened successfully and shows the opening line “clean heat and electricity to power a world of industrial applications,” the vision and mission sections, the Zettajoule naming story, and three offices: Rotterdam (Headquarters), Chicago (Licensing), and Tokyo (Engineering).

claims.substep_do: Open the technology route and confirm the cutaway with the fuel, the graphite, the helium, the digital copy, the safety case and the modules
claims.observation: The Technology route opened and shows the reactor cutaway plus sections for The fuel, The graphite, The helium, The Digital Twin (living copy), The Safety Case, and Modules.

claims.substep_do: Drag the technology diagram, then tap one part, and confirm that part explains itself
claims.observation: Turned the technology diagram from position 0 to 1, then tapped “Helium coolant”; the page displayed an explanation that helium is inert, remains a gas, and enables the 750-degree outlet.

claims.substep_do: Open the edge route and confirm the modernized proven design, the temperature case, the modules and the business model
claims.observation: The /edge route clearly presents the proven reactor modernized with current materials/instrumentation, the 320°C vs 750°C temperature case, scalable identical modules, and the owner-operated energy-sales business model.

claims.substep_do: Open the team route and confirm the opening line over a grid of four leaders on soft tinted plates
claims.observation: The /team route opens with “shaping the future of nuclear together” above four leader entries—Mira Halvorsen, Tobias Ruiz, Anneke Vos, and Daniel Okoye—laid out in a four-column row on generated portrait plates.

claims.substep_do: Open one leader profile link, then the view-bio action, and confirm the fuller description opens in the shared modal
claims.observation: Opened Mira Halvorsen’s profile link, returned to the team page, then used View bio; the shared modal opened with her full role heading, extended biography, Close control, and Professional profile link.

claims.substep_do: Move between two showcase routes and confirm the change does not reload the page and a cover sweeps across
claims.observation: Navigating Company → Technology → Solutions used client-side route transitions: the destination title/content changed before the URL commit, then the URL updated without a document reload, and the app’s transition cover swept between routes.

claims.substep_do: Open the home route with scripting turned off and confirm the whole page arrives as complete HTML, then turn scripting back on and confirm only the filter row, the save control and the modals become interactive
claims.observation: The server does return a complete HTML home page (HTTP 200 with all major page content present before JavaScript), but the hydrated home route has no filter row, save control, or modals; it instead exposes ordinary navigation/content links, so the requested interactive-enhancement claim cannot be co

claims.substep_do: Confirm the bars, the words and the first view of the reactor are usable before the whole sequence has arrived, and that the heavier extras arrive only on reaching them
claims.observation: The initial view exposed usable navigation bars, hero copy, reactor metrics/first-view content, and a complete textual description of the reactor sequence; network activity then increased only after scrolling into later content, consistent with heavier extras being deferred until reached.

claims.substep_do: Narrow the browser to a phone width and confirm the menu button opens a full panel
claims.observation: At a 390×844 phone viewport, tapping “Open menu” set aria-expanded=true and opened a full-width mobile panel with a Close menu control and navigation links spanning the 350px content width.

claims.substep_do: Open an address that was never a route and confirm the not-found card reads We cannot find that page and links home
claims.observation: The never-defined route displays the not-found card heading “We cannot find that page” and includes a “Back to the home route” link with href="/".

claims.substep_do: Open the solutions route and confirm eight industry cards in a grid under a filter row offering an industry choice
claims.observation: The /solutions route shows a filter row with an Industry selector ('All industries' plus eight industry choices), followed by 'Showing 8 of 8 solutions' and eight industry cards arranged in a four-column grid.

claims.substep_do: Choose the hydrogen output and the top temperature band, then confirm the count reads two of eight
claims.observation: Selected Hydrogen output and the top temperature band (550 to 750 C); the page confirms “Showing 2 of 8 solutions.”

claims.substep_do: Open one industry card and confirm the solution explains what the reactor does for that industry block by block
claims.observation: Opened the Steel industry card; its solution page explains the reactor’s role for steel and includes a clear five-step “Block by block” sequence covering Core, Hot header, Exchange, Delivery, and Return leg.

claims.substep_do: Confirm the opened solution offers a save action and an enquire action
claims.observation: The opened Steel solution displays both a “Save Steel” button and an “Enquire about Steel” button.

claims.substep_do: Return to the home route and follow one of the four output links, then confirm the explorer arrives already filtered to that output
claims.observation: Returned via the Zettajoule home link, followed the home page’s Hydrogen output link, and the explorer opened pre-filtered to Hydrogen, showing 2 of 8 matching solutions (Transport and Steel).

claims.substep_do: Search the explorer in plain language and confirm the grid narrows to matching industries
claims.observation: Entered the plain-language search “hydrogen”; the explorer narrowed from 8 solutions to 2 matching industries, Transport and Steel, both showing Hydrogen output.

claims.substep_do: Confirm the solutions grid also reads as a plain written list
claims.observation: The solutions grid exposes each visible card as plain text with an industry name and written description (Steel, Data Centres, Chemicals, Desalination, Mining, and Communities), so it reads coherently as a written list without relying on imagery.

claims.substep_do: With no account, save one industry solution and confirm the result appears in place as a banner
claims.observation: While signed out, saving Oil and Gas updated the button to “Saved Oil and Gas” and displayed the in-place banner “Oil and Gas saved. Sign in and it follows you in.”

claims.substep_do: Sign up from the same browser and confirm the saved solution is waiting on the account route
claims.observation: Created a new account in the same browser, opened /account, and confirmed the anonymous saved solution was claimed: Saved solutions shows 1, Oil and Gas.

claims.substep_do: Confirm the account route lists the enquiries sent with the state of each
claims.observation: The account route lists the sent enquiry ENQ-YR6E7VMP under Enquiries, including its topic/date and current state “received”.

claims.substep_do: Open the comparison route with four saved solutions and confirm four columns side by side
claims.observation: Opened /compare?slugs=oil-and-gas,chemicals,transport,steel; it shows “4 of 4 compared” and the four solution columns (Oil and Gas, Chemicals, Transport, Steel) aligned side by side.

claims.substep_do: Add a fifth saved solution and confirm the refusal appears in place while four are still compared
claims.observation: Attempting to add Mining as the fifth comparison showed an in-place refusal message, while the count remained 4 of 4 and Oil and Gas, Chemicals, Transport, and Steel remained compared.

claims.substep_do: Open the contact route and confirm the explanation of what the form serves over the six fields
claims.observation: The contact route opens with an explanation above six fields: the form serves careers, investor, and supplier enquiries, plus sites wanting to discuss heat, power, hydrogen, or water; it also says submissions receive an emailed acknowledgement with a reference.

claims.substep_do: Send the enquiry and confirm the reference appears in place
claims.observation: Enquiry sent successfully; the in-place confirmation shows reference ENQ-PG76JR1B and says its status is received.

claims.substep_do: Open the investors route and confirm the energy need, the business case, the dated roadmap and the pending notice
claims.observation: Investors route shows the industrial energy need, the long-contract owned-and-operated business case, a dated 1998–2031 roadmap, and the pending access notice stating approval happens outside the product.

claims.substep_do: Request investor access and confirm the account route reads the request as pending
claims.observation: Investor access is requested, and the account route shows reference IAR-9T3V6BLM for Northwind Industrial / Head of Strategy with status “pending.”

claims.substep_do: Sign in as the approved account, open the document room and confirm the three documents are listed
claims.observation: Signed in as approved account Ada Moreau, opened the private document room, and confirmed all three documents are listed: Investor Deck 2026, Technology Dossier, and Licensing Roadmap.

claims.substep_do: Sign in as the pending account, open the same address and confirm the not-found page
claims.observation: Signed in as the pending account Ken Adeyemi (visitor2@example.com), opened the Document room address, and confirmed the not-found page stating “We cannot find that page” because access is not approved.

claims.substep_do: Sign in as the second account and confirm the account route lists only that account own saves
claims.observation: Signed in as visitor2@example.com (Ken Adeyemi); the account view shows exactly one saved solution, Mining, with no other saves listed.

claims.substep_do: Confirm the account route lists only that account own enquiries and its own access request
claims.observation: The account route is signed in as Ken Adeyemi and shows only one enquiry (ENQ-5R8X1CJ2) plus that account’s single investor access request (IAR-9T3V6BLM for Northwind Industrial); no other enquiries or access requests are listed.

claims.substep_do: With no session, open the account route and confirm the browser lands on the sign-in route carrying the return path
claims.observation: With cookies cleared, opening /account displayed the sign-in page and said “Sign in to continue to /account,” but the browser URL remained /account rather than landing on a /signin route with the return path in the URL.

claims.substep_do: Sign in from there and confirm the browser lands back on the account route
claims.observation: Signed in successfully as visitor@example.com and the browser landed on the /account route.

claims.substep_do: Clear the session mid-visit and confirm the next protected route sends the visitor back to sign in
claims.observation: Cleared the active session mid-visit, then opened the protected document-room route; the app returned the visitor to the Sign in page with “Sign in to continue to /investors/room.”

claims.substep_do: Open the calculator route, enter a thermal need and confirm the module count, the energy figure and the carbon figure appear beside a simple bar chart
claims.observation: On /calculator, entering 251 MW and selecting Thermal produced 2 modules, 4,000 GWh annual clean energy, and 1,800,000 tonnes annual carbon avoided, with the corresponding labeled chart figures displayed.

claims.substep_do: Enter a need one megawatt over a whole module and confirm the module count rises by one
claims.observation: Entered a 251 MW thermal need—1 MW above one 250 MW module—and the calculator returned 2 modules required, confirming the count rose by one.

claims.substep_do: Open the newsroom and confirm the heading over one featured story raised above a wall of three cards, each with a plate and where it ran
claims.observation: Opened the Newsroom: featured heading “First module order signed” is raised above a three-card row; each card has a visual plate and identifies where it ran—Company news, Industry Week, and Energy Monitor.

claims.substep_do: Press the more action and confirm the next three stories arrive
claims.observation: Pressed “More stories”; the next three stories appeared, and the page now shows 6 of 6 stories.

claims.substep_do: Open one story and confirm the full text
claims.observation: Opened the featured “First module order signed” story and confirmed its full article text is displayed.

claims.substep_do: Open the careers route and confirm the heading, the culture story, the three open jobs and the Operations Academy
claims.observation: Careers route opened and shows the heading “help us build what's next in nuclear energy,” the “How it works here” culture story, the Operations Academy section, and exactly three open jobs: Reactor Systems Engineer, Licensing Lead, and Operations Trainer.

claims.substep_do: Press apply on one job and confirm the short form opens in the shared modal
claims.observation: Pressed Apply for Reactor Systems Engineer; the shared modal opened with the short application form (name, email, note, and Send application).

claims.substep_do: Confirm the apply form offers no file input and no attachment control
claims.observation: The open apply form contains only name, email, and note fields plus a Send application button; it explicitly states “There is no attachment,” and no file input or attachment control is present.

claims.substep_do: Open the questions route and confirm the searchable list of common questions
claims.observation: Opened the Common questions/FAQ route and confirmed it shows six common questions with a search field and category filter; searching “helium” narrowed the list to two matching questions.

evidence: On /solutions, selecting the Output filter value “Hydrogen” changed the result count from “Showing 8 of 8 solutions” to “Showing 2 of 8 solutions” and replaced the eight-card grid with only Transport and Steel.

A CDP motion capture started immediately before that filter selection and stopped after the updated count appeared recorded animation_count=0, directly showing no fade, slide, or stagger during grid replacement.
Computed styles on a resulting grid item showed transition-property:none, transition-duration:0s, animation-name:none, animation-duration:0s, opacity:1, and transform:none.

Separate CDP captures of focusing controls recorded exactly two 120 ms ease-out animations—outline-color and outline-offset—while the focused select had a solid 3px blue outline. Focusing the search field produced the same two outline animations.
A second filter selection (“Multi module”) likewise settled with animation_count=0.
active_results.rationale: The filter result lands immediately without grid animation, while focused controls retain a short animated focus ring. This directly satisfies the positive motion requirement.

evidence: At 1920×1200 on route /, the top-row brand link “Zettajoule” occupied x=370–501, y=13–49; route links ran from “Company” at x=495–568, y=13–49 through “Contact” at x=1156–1230, y=13–49; the sole header “Get in Touch” occupied x=1419–1550, y=12–50. These aligned bounding boxes directly establish a slim horizontal top bar rather than a side rail.

The / snapshot exposed exactly nine header route labels: Company, Technology, Solutions, Our Edge, Our Team, Investors, News, Careers, and Contact, followed by one header Get in Touch action. The brand was identified as class “brand”, aria-label “Zettajoule, home”, href “/”; the action linked to “/contact”.

After scrolling from the top to PageDown and then End, the brand and Get in Touch bounding boxes remained unchanged at y≈12–50 and visible, directly supporting that the bar is fixed/sticky during page scrolling.
Navigation to /company retained the same header contents: Zettajoule, all nine route labels, and one top-bar Get in Touch action, showing the layout persists across the tested route transition.

Supplied deterministic geometry independently records the header wrapper “bar-inner” as display:flex with three horizontal children at x=370, 519, and 1223, plus the route-list ul as display:flex with nine children and the header action link class “get-in-touch”.
verdicts.rationale: Direct snapshots, route transition, scroll behavior, computed visibility, and measured bounding boxes establish a slim fixed horizontal top bar containing the Zettajoule logo/brand lockup, route labels, and one header Get in Touch action. Navigation is horizontal rather than in a side rail. Although another Get in Touch exists later in the page/footer, the criterion’s singular action is clearly satisfied within the top bar.

Repeated first-visit navigations to / (using fresh query strings) returned only after the completed page was already visible, with the hero text “Powering the World” and the reactor-sequence description present.
Immediate snapshots after navigation showed the full homepage; they did not expose the transient initial loading state.
Direct waits immediately after separate reloads found no visible “Loading”, “%”, or “Preparing” text within 1 second.

Animation capture consistently observed one running 1700 ms infinite pulse animation, but the available evidence does not identify its element or prove that it is a white progress cover that lifts only after reactor readiness.
verdicts.rationale: The browser navigation primitive does not provide a pre-load frame, and the transient cover—if present—had already disappeared by the time each navigation call returned. Therefore I could not directly verify the required white cover, its progress readout, or the ordering between cover removal and the reactor’s first render. Per the evaluation instruction, this missing evidence is not treated as a failure.

evidence: On the authenticated /account route, after removing the final saved solution through its confirmation dialog, the persisted zero state read: “Saved solutions 0”, “Nothing saved yet”, “Save a card in the explorer and it lands here.” and offered the “Open the explorer” link.

After removing the final saved search through its confirmation dialog, the persisted zero state read: “Saved searches 0”, “No saved search”, “Filter the explorer and save that combination under a name.” and offered the “Go and filter” link.

The account already had no applications, and its empty state read: “Job applications 0”, “No application sent”, “Apply to an open job and it appears here with its status.” and offered the “See open jobs” link.
A direct reload of /account preserved all three zero states and their explanatory onward links, confirming these were rendered account states rather than transient notices.
verdicts.rationale: The required account state—no saves, no searches, and no applications—was directly established and verified after reload. Every empty list explicitly names what is absent and provides a clear route onward; none renders as blank space.
